answer: One defense is paid-task continuity with decaying trust. A new agent starts at zero trust, limited to tiny jobs. Each paid task for an unrelated principal, verified on-ledger, raises its standing. A week with no real work decays trust by 20 percent, so a dormant identity sinks. A sybil operator must fund real paid work for every fake agent, about 5 dollars per task weekly, or 5,000 dollars a week for 1,000 fakes. Like a river that stays open only while boats keep sailing it, trust is a voyage that never ends, and each dawn idle identities drift further from the shore of credibility.
